### 1. Scene
A mixed plate with an Asian pear, a slice of bread spread with red jam, roasted chicken pieces, and a small breaded fried chicken piece.

### 2. Vessel
A round dinner plate, approximately **26 cm** across.  
Area = 3.14 × 13² = **531 cm²**.

### 3–7. Items, area, volume, weight, and energy
Heights below are average heights across each item's footprint, rather than maximum heights. Chicken estimates include visible bones; their energy densities are correspondingly lower than boneless meat.

| Item | Plate area covered | Area × average height = gross volume | Bulk density | Estimated weight | kcal/100 g | Energy |
|---|---:|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Whole Asian pear | 12% | 64 cm² × 4.1 cm = 262 ml | 0.80 | 210 g | 42 | 88 kcal |
| Bread slice | 16% | 85 cm² × 1.5 cm = 128 ml | 0.30 | 38 g | 265 | 101 kcal |
| Red jam | 10%, overlapping bread | 53 cm² × 0.35 cm = 19 ml | 1.00 | 19 g | 250 | 48 kcal |
| Roasted chicken leg piece, skin-on | 12% | 64 cm² × 1.9 cm = 122 ml | 0.95 | 116 g | 185 | 215 kcal |
| Small roasted chicken wing piece | 4% | 21 cm² × 1.5 cm = 32 ml | 0.95 | 30 g | 180 | 54 kcal |
| Breaded fried chicken piece | 6% | 32 cm² × 1.6 cm = 51 ml | 0.90 | 46 g | 290 | 133 kcal |

The food footprints cover approximately **50% of the plate**. Jam overlaps the bread, so its coverage is not added again. No separate pool of oil or additional sauce is visible; cooking fat is included in the chicken energy estimates.

### 8. Sanity check
The estimate is **459 g and approximately 640 kcal**, including the pear core and chicken bones. That is plausible for one large whole fruit, one slice of bread with jam, and three modest chicken pieces. Edible weight would be somewhat lower.
